primary_sources: Rollin Kirby, 'Classroom in Proposed Bryan University of Tennessee,' 1925

stimulus.text: The cartoon shows a classroom. A teacher, tied with ropes and gagged, points with a stick at a wall chart titled “MAP OF THE EARTH.” The chart shows a flat strip of land marked “AMERICA,” “BRITISH ISLES,” “EUROPE,” and “ASIA,” with the space below it labeled “VOID.” A framed portrait labeled “PREXY” hangs on the wall, and a second chart labeled “HELL” shows flames. Two students watch from desks below. The caption reads: “CLASSROOM IN PROPOSED BRYAN UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE.” — Rollin Kirby, 1925.
stimulus.source_note: Rollin Kirby, “Classroom in Proposed Bryan University of Tennessee,” 1925. Public domain (published 1925, pre-1930); via Wikimedia Commons.

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Rollin Kirby cartoon, 1925, public domain
stem: The cartoon suggests that a university run on William Jennings Bryan's ideas would teach students that

options.text: modern science should guide all teaching
options.misconception: The cartoon shows science silenced, not guiding teaching. The gagged teacher and the flat-earth chart point the other way.

options.text: the Bible and Darwin can both be taught
options.misconception: The cartoon shows only one view allowed. The teacher is gagged, so Darwin's ideas cannot be taught at all.

options.text: the earth is flat and evolution is false
teachers should choose their own lessons
options.misconception: The cartoon shows the teacher bound and gagged. He cannot choose his lessons; the portrait on the wall decides what is taught.

rationales.A: The cartoon shows science silenced, not guiding teaching. The gagged teacher and the flat-earth chart point the other way.
rationales.B: The cartoon shows only one view allowed. The teacher is gagged, so Darwin's ideas cannot be taught at all.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the chart shows a flat earth with a void below it, and the gagged teacher cannot teach anything else. A school run on Bryan's ideas would teach the flat earth and reject evolution.
rationales.D: The cartoon shows the teacher bound and gagged. He cannot choose his lessons; the portrait on the wall decides what is taught.
rationales.general:
1. Look at what the teacher can show: a flat earth over a void.
2. Look at what he cannot do: he is tied and gagged. Background: the trial was over teaching evolution, so the gag silences that teaching.
3. Read the caption: this is Bryan's proposed university in Tennessee.
4. Put it together: the cartoonist says Bryan's school would teach the Bible's account and silence science.
Remember: in a cartoon, what the artist takes away from a figure tells you the argument.
